![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14186989/assets/635de7075b0d106ffc2a0f15e65ca7a3406a49945591aa5eae59090c74df1398.png)

Due to the symmetry of the student's $t$-distribution, we have that $P(|X|\ge x)=0.05$ is equivalent to

$$
2P(X\ge x)=0.05\,⟹\,P(X\ge x)=0.025.
$$

Now, since $X∼{T}_{11},$ we focus on the row of the table that corresponds to $k=11.$

| $k∖p$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.010$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $10$ | $1.372$ | $1.812$ | $2.228$ | $2.764$ | $3.169$ |
| $11$ | $1.363$ | $1.796$ | $2.201$ | $2.718$ | $3.106$ |
| $12$ | $1.356$ | $1.782$ | $2.179$ | $2.681$ | $3.055$ |

From this row, we see that

$$
P(X\ge 2.201)=0.025.
$$

Therefore, our answer is $x=2.201.$
